header.author: Achilles Tatius

nodes.text: And she cried out, and the girl jumped up, set down her lyre, examined the sting, and at the same time comforted her, telling her not to be upset: she would stop her pain by chanting two words over it; for she had been taught them by an Egyptian woman, for the stings of wasps and bees.

For if one presses it against a body, it retreats into the handle as into a sheath; and the onlookers think the iron is being plunged into the body, but it has run back up into the hollow of the handle and leaves only the point, enough to cut the false belly, while the hilt meets the skin of the one being slaughtered; and if one pulls the iron out of the wound, the blade slides back down out of the hollow by as much as the raised part of the handle is lifted, and in the same way deceives the onlookers.

Being a poisoner by nature, he prepares a love drug and persuades the Egyptian who serves you to take the drug and mix it into Leucippe’s drink. But without realising it he used the drug undiluted, and the love charm rose into madness.
